title: Large Language Models Have Not Yet Transformed Science
abstract: arXiv:2611.22975v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The emergence of large language models (LLMs) in late 2022 has raised questions about the future of science, but assessing their impact requires understanding how scientific practices were already evolving. We analyze 2.5 million full-text papers across five disciplines from 2015 to 2025, tracing trends over a broad spectrum of lexical, structural, epistemological, and social dimensions. Aside from frequency shifts in some words, most pre-2023 trends continued with limited detectable breaks. Among the notable exceptions, growth in computer science coauthor teams accelerated significantly in Asia, while apparent declines in biomedical topic diversity largely reflected standardization in article formats. Our study establishes an empirical foundation for monitoring the health of global science as LLM adoption deepens.

translated_title: 大语言模型尚未改变科学
translated_abstract: 2022年底大语言模型（LLMs）的出现引发了对科学未来的诸多疑问，但要评估其影响，需要理解科学实践此前是如何演变的。我们分析了2015年至2025年间五个学科的250万篇全文论文，在词汇、结构、认识论和社会等多个维度上追踪了广泛的变化趋势。除了一些词汇频率的变化外，大多数2023年之前的趋势仍在延续，可检测到的中断十分有限。在少数显著的例外中，亚洲计算机科学领域合作团队的快速增长明显加速，而生物医学领域主题多样性的明显下降则主要反映了论文格式的标准化。我们的研究为在大语言模型应用日益深入的背景下监测全球科学的健康状况奠定了实证基础。
tldr: 该研究通过分析2015至2025年间五个学科250万篇全文论文发现，除个别例外，大语言模型出现后科学实践的大多数既有趋势仍在延续，表明LLM尚未从根本上改变科学研究的方式。
en_tdlr: By analyzing 2.5 million full-text papers across five disciplines from 2015 to 2025, this study finds that most pre-existing trends in scientific practice continued after LLMs emerged, indicating that LLMs have not yet fundamentally transformed science.
